blocks.html: This proof also was not very conclusive: for it often happens that true and legitimate children take after a stranger better than their natural father, as we have shown above. Wherefore I shall content myself for the present with referring the reader to what Plutarch has written of it.

notes.citation: Pseudo-Plutarch, De placitis philosophorum (Placita philosophorum, in the Moralia), book 5 — chapters 11–12, why children resemble their parents or their ancestors, and how they come to resemble others rather than their parents (chapter not cited)
notes.original: Plutarque au liure v. de placit. Philoſ.
notes.gloss: Printed beside "renuoyer le lecteur à ce"; it evidently serves the sentence that refers the reader to Plutarch.
